execution.session_policy: New Chromium contexts for authenticated and anonymous users in each run
execution.restart_policy: No service restart or automatic test retry; run twice with fresh owned fixtures

side_effect_policy.target: Confirmed loopback Artifact Center instance only
side_effect_policy.fixture_setup: Create one uniquely named ZIP Application in an existing enabled Product and Project
side_effect_policy.publish: Beta only, inside the owned Application
side_effect_policy.download: Allowed to ignored local evidence directory
side_effect_policy.share: Local fixed-version link, one-day expiry; no external delivery
side_effect_policy.personal_preferences: Capture before browser filtering; restore and verify in finally
side_effect_policy.cleanup: Registered ID plus current run name check; never delete pre-existing data
side_effect_policy.audit: Append-only facts remain according to product behavior

preconditions: Healthy local instance and externally supplied local admin credentials
actions: Enter credentials in the browser login form and sign in
expected: Authenticated application page is visible and the session can access the current user endpoint

evidence.assertion: Login route leaves /login, Applications heading is visible, /auth/me confirms cleanup authority

preconditions: An owned Application has been registered by ID and unique run name
actions: Type the unique application name into browser search and open its result
expected: One matching result opens the detail route for the registered application ID

evidence.assertion: Unique result count, detail URL and exact application heading match

preconditions: Owned ZIP application and generated valid ZIP fixture
actions: Select the fixture, edit version/build, explicitly select Beta, review and publish through the browser
expected: Published artifact belongs to the owned application and preserves version, build, Beta channel, file size and SHA-256
Artifact history displays the published version and Beta/Latest state

evidence.assertion: Real upload completion response matches the source ZIP metadata, success UI and artifact history agree

preconditions: Owned Beta artifact has been published
actions: Click the artifact download button and confirm the test-version notice
expected: Downloaded distribution filename, byte length and SHA-256 match the published artifact and source ZIP

evidence.assertion: Native browser download compared with source; a toast alone is not accepted

actions: Create a pinned share with one-day expiry in the browser
Open the link in a new unauthenticated browser context and confirm download
expected: Anonymous page shows the owned application and Beta channel
Downloaded file has the same distribution filename, byte length and SHA-256

evidence.assertion: Separate context without copied auth state completes the actual file download and digest check

preconditions: Fixture ownership entries and original inventory/workspace snapshots recorded
actions: Finally verify registered application ID and current run name, delete it, and verify artifact and share invalidation
Restore original workspace preferences and compare pre-existing inventory and workspace state
expected: Owned application and artifact are unavailable, owned share is invalid, original inventory and workspace agree with baseline

evidence.assertion: 404 checks, invalid-share page, inventory comparison and workspace comparison are recorded

cleanup: Delete only the application whose ID and current run name both match the registry
Retain mismatch evidence; never broaden cleanup to unrelated applications

scope_exclusions: Stable production publication and real APK/AAB/EXE installation packages
Viewer/maintainer permission matrix and invalid authentication
Interrupted upload, resume, retry, concurrent publication and storage quota boundaries
Latest-mode and collection shares, expiry and explicit revocation
Other browsers, mobile layout, accessibility, visual regression and CI environment provisioning
scope_note: This matrix covers the bounded core workflow authorized in this task. Implemented means runnable assertions, not a recorded passing run; inspect the run evidence for the actual verdict.
